# Collective-Intelligence @ Stage 5 — Sensory-Motor

> developed 2026-07-26. Deepened from 73 to 140+ lines.

## Expression on this line

Collective-intelligence at Order 3 is **impulsive collective competition**: the agent
has a self that wants collective power, and it will take it by force, deception, or
speed if it can. There are no rules about collective behavior — only the raw dynamic
of "I see what I want in the group and I take it."

The key advance from Stage 4 is **instrumental collective behavior**. The agent does
not just claim collective configurations it stumbles upon — it actively seeks out
collective power, plans simple collective acquisition strategies, and adjusts its
behavior based on what works. A child who learns that joining the right group produces
social advantages is using instrumental behavior as a collective strategy.

At Stage 5, the agent begins to follow **external rules** about collective behavior,
but only when监督 is present. The rule is not internalized — it is an external constraint.

Collective competition at Stage 5 is **zero-sum** in the agent's perception. If I have
more collective power, you have less. There is no concept of collaborative collective
creation.

The transition from Stage 5 to Stage 6 occurs when collective rules become internalized.

In human development, Stage 5 corresponds to the preschooler who grabs group
membership, hoards collective power, and cries when others have more. But also begins
to learn "sharing rules" when监督 is present.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** The first social collective rules emerge, though externally enforced. "Don't
  exclude other kids" is a Stage 5 collective norm.

- **UR:** The individual agent exhibits instrumental collective behavior. It can plan
  simple collective acquisition strategies and adjust its approach.

- **LL:** Surveillance-based collective institutions emerge. The teacher who monitors
  group dynamics, the parent who supervises play.

- **LR:** The agent's body as social actor, the group as territory, the监督 as
  external rule.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** Compulsive collective aggression — taking group power not because
  the agent needs it but because the act of dominating produces satisfaction.

- **Dark allergy:** Failure to engage in collective competition at all.

- **Golden addiction:** Clinging to the zero-sum perception of collective power.

- **Golden allergy:** Rejecting all collective competition as inherently wrong.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Instrumental collective behavior:** The agent uses tactics to acquire group power
  beyond passive reception.

- **监督-dependent rule following:** The agent follows collective rules only when
  监督 is present.

- **Zero-sum collective perception:** The agent perceives collective exchanges as
  win-lose.

- **Territorial collective defense:** The agent defends claimed group positions through
  aggression or deception.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:**
- Piaget, J. (1952). *The Origins of Intelligence in Children* — sensory-motor
  foundations of collective behavior
- Tomasello, M. (1999). *The Cultural Origins of Human Cognition* — from individual
  to shared collective strategies
- Wilson, E.O. (1975). *Sociobiology* — the evolutionary foundations of collective
  competition
